analysis.title: GS Novak - GS U.S. Industrials & Materials | EPS review 28 Oct 2026
key_insights: Desk sees a heavy earnings day with AI-related names looking to trade better broadly. GEV was the most discussed name pre-market with feedback mostly mixed to negative, while VRT was the standout positive though terminal value debates remain.

Residential HVAC is weak across the board, highlighted by LII's full-year guide down. Pool end markets are finding a bottom, with HAYW the latest example. PPG feedback is mixed because Q4 is below prior thinking despite a Q3 beat. IP is becoming an idiosyncratic story.
Desk pre-market trading perspective. Better: AER CLH FTV HAYW IEX IP KEX LFUS MAS TEL VRT. Worse: DAN LII PSN SITE SW. Mixed: CHRW GEV GNRC ODFL OTIS TEX.

GEV Q3 revenue was $12.64bn vs $12bn consensus and EBITDA $1.94bn vs $1.68bn. Full-year guide raised to sales $47bn (consensus $46bn), EBITDA $6.6bn (consensus $6.34bn) and free cash flow $16-17bn. Buyback boosted to $20bn from $10bn, and a $9bn Trench Group acquisition was announced. Desk feedback is that slot reservations of 11GW came in below the 10-15GW expectation, with a preference for other AI names coming out of today.

VRT Q3 EPS was $2.21 vs $1.82 consensus on revenue of $4.3bn vs $3.75bn. Americas organic growth accelerated to 66%, with orders up 100%. Americas margins were below consensus. Q4 guide of $2.22-2.28 EPS is slightly ahead of $2.21 consensus. Desk calls it the most oversold of the AI/data center industrials.

LII Q3 EPS was $6.84 vs $7.36 consensus. Full-year EPS guide cut to $21-21.50 from $23-24, revenue growth to 6% from 8%, and free cash flow to $700-750mm from $750-850mm. Desk expects the stock to trade off on revisions, noting the company skipped conferences and residential trends have been weak.

AER Q3 EPS was $6.56 vs $4.56 on revenue of $2.42bn vs $2.15bn, with $783mm of buybacks in the quarter. Full-year guide was raised to $20.70 from $16.80, partly driven by gains on sale. Desk says headlines are driven by gains but EPS continues to grind higher.

DAN Q3 EPS was $0.41 vs $0.70 consensus despite a sales beat of $2.04bn vs $1.96bn. Full-year EPS guide cut to $1.75-2.25 from $2-3. Desk says the big guide down will offset the help from the buyback re-engagement.

SW Q3 EBITDA was $1.21bn vs $1.3bn consensus on revenue of $8.16bn vs $8.26bn, with North America missing on revenue and margins. Full-year EBITDA is now about $4.7bn vs $4.9-5.1bn prior. Desk expects positioning in a crowded materials name to weigh.

TEL fiscal Q4 EPS was $3.14 vs $3.07. Fiscal Q1 guide is well ahead at EPS $3.30 vs $3 and revenue $5.35bn vs $5.14bn. Desk says expectations are much lower than in a while and the guide should ease concerns.

Several names beat and raised: FTV (guide $3.10-3.14 vs $2.95-3.05), IEX (full-year EPS $8.91-8.96 vs $8.70-8.85), MAS (full-year EPS $4.65-4.75 vs $4.40-4.60), HAYW (full-year EPS $0.86-0.88 vs $0.84-0.87), LFUS (Q4 EPS guide above $5.05-5.25 vs $4.16 consensus), CLH (raised full-year EBITDA). Desk flags low sentiment at FTV and negative positioning at MAS as setups for a positive reaction.

Mixed or in-line prints: GNRC beat on EPS ($2.54 vs $2.43) but missed on revenue ($1.29bn vs $1.32bn) and raised margin guidance, and desk says the bar was set high. OTIS beat EPS ($1.05 vs $1.01) but cut free cash flow to the low end of $1.5bn, and desk is unsure what will excite investors. SITE was in line at $1.46 EPS with a lower full-year EBITDA midpoint, and desk says crowding has turned negative but the beat is unlikely to spark covering. PSN beat but desk sees no flow-through.

CHRW EPS of $1.80 vs $1.75 on revenue of $5.4bn vs $4.93bn, with desk saying one quarter is hard to change the narrative around the deal. ODFL EBIT of $453mm vs $446mm, with the stock hinging on October and Q4 commentary on the call and implied September tonnage turning positive.

IP Q3 EPS was $0.37 vs $0.29 and EBITDA $843mm vs $784mm. Desk expects it to stick out positively against peers. KEX EPS of $2.09 vs $2 on revenue of $977mm vs $939mm, with desk noting it is well owned. TEX EPS of $1.50 vs $1.42 with a new $500mm buyback, and desk says it is still a waiting portfolio.

earnings_insights: AER Q3 EPS reported $6.56 vs consensus $4.56 on revenue $2.42bn vs $2.15bn consensus. Full-year EPS guide raised to $20.70 from $16.80 prior, partly from gains on sale. Reported 10/28 pre-market.
CHRW Q3 EPS reported $1.80 vs consensus $1.75, revenue $5.4bn vs $4.93bn, gross profit $808mm vs $774mm. Reported 10/28.
CLH Q3 EBITDA reported $456mm vs consensus $408mm on revenue $1.87bn vs $1.73bn. Full-year EBITDA forecast raised. Eric Gerstenber named CEO.
DAN Q3 EPS reported $0.41 vs consensus $0.70, sales $2.04bn vs $1.96bn. Full-year EPS guide lowered to $1.75-2.25 from $2-3. Sales guide $7.75-7.85bn vs $7.65-7.85bn prior.
FTV Q3 EPS reported $0.77 vs consensus $0.70, sales $1.11bn vs $1.07bn. Full-year EPS guide raised to $3.10-3.14 from $2.95-3.05.

GEV Q3 revenue reported $12.64bn vs consensus $12bn, EBITDA $1.94bn vs $1.68bn, EPS $4.81 vs consensus $4.01 (the report prints this as $4.01bn). Full-year guide: sales $47bn (consensus $46bn), EBITDA $6.6bn (consensus $6.34bn), free cash flow $16-17bn. Buyback raised to $20bn from $10bn. Trench Group acquisition for $9bn, with $0.5bn of 2026 EBITDA and $0.6bn of 2027 EBITDA.

GNRC Q3 EPS reported $2.54 vs consensus $2.43, revenue $1.29bn vs $1.32bn, EBITDA $256mm vs $253mm. Residential revenue $744mm vs $753mm, C&I $553mm vs $583mm. Margin guide raised to the high end of 20.5-21% from 20-21%.
HAYW Q3 EPS reported $0.18 vs consensus $0.15, sales $260mm vs $252mm. Full-year EPS guide $0.86-0.88 from $0.84-0.87, sales growth 5-6%.
IEX Q3 EPS reported $2.33 vs consensus $2.24, sales $952mm vs $932mm, EBITDA $265mm. Full-year EPS guide $8.91-8.96 from $8.70-8.85, organic growth +6.5-6.8% from +5-6%.
IP Q3 EPS reported $0.37 vs consensus $0.29, sales $6.2bn, EBITDA $843mm vs $784mm. Q4 Packaging Solutions guide: segment operating profit $460-500mm, EBITDA $700-740mm.
KEX Q3 EPS reported $2.09 vs consensus $2.00, revenue $977mm vs $939mm. EPS growth guide now upper end of 10-15% y/y vs upper end of 5-15% prior. Cash from operations guide $575-675mm.
LFUS Q3 EBITDA reported $226mm vs consensus $204mm, sales $767mm vs $792mm, EPS $5.79 vs $4.97. Q4 EPS guide above $5.05-5.25 vs consensus $4.16 (as printed in the report).

LII Q3 EPS reported $6.84 vs consensus $7.36, revenue $1.57bn in line. Full-year EPS guide $21-21.50 from $23-24, revenue growth 6% from 8%, free cash flow $700-750mm from $750-850mm. HCS revenue $937mm vs $963mm, EBIT $176mm vs $211mm. BCS revenue $635mm vs $603mm, EBIT $167mm vs $157mm.

MAS Q3 EPS reported $1.19 vs consensus $1.02, revenue $1.97bn vs $1.93bn, EBIT $351mm vs $316mm. Full-year EPS guide $4.65-4.75 from $4.40-4.60. Plumbing Products revenue $1.34bn vs $1.29bn, Decorative Architectural $628mm in line.
ODFL Q3 EBIT reported $453mm vs consensus $446mm, sales $1.59bn vs $1.57bn. October and Q4 updates on the call are the focus.

OTIS Q3 EPS reported $1.05 vs consensus $1.01, sales $3.91bn vs $3.85bn, EBIT $626mm vs $617mm. Organic sales +6% driven by service. Revenue and EPS guidance reaffirmed, free cash flow lowered to the low end of $1.5bn from $1.5-1.55bn.

PSN Q3 EPS reported $0.89 vs consensus $0.78, revenue $1.7bn vs $1.6bn. Federal Solutions revenue $805mm vs $775mm with margin 11.1% vs 8.7%. Critical Infrastructure revenue $846mm in line with margin 11.7% vs 10.7%. Book to bill 1.1x. Full-year revenue guide narrowed to $6.258-6.45bn from $6.2-6.5bn, EBITDA $510-550mm from $500-560mm, cash from operations $430-490mm reiterated.
SITE Q3 EPS reported $1.46 in line, revenue $1.29bn in line, organic sales down 1%, EBITDA $138mm vs $133mm. Full-year EBITDA guide $425-440mm from $425-455mm.

SW Q3 EBITDA reported $1.21bn vs consensus $1.3bn, revenue $8.16bn vs $8.26bn, EPS below $0.45 vs $0.57. North America revenue $4.75bn vs $4.92bn, margin 15.6% vs 16.8%. Full-year EBITDA about $4.7bn vs $4.9-5.1bn prior.

TEL fiscal Q4 EPS reported $3.14 vs consensus $3.07, revenue $5.31bn vs $5.29bn. Fiscal Q1 guide: EPS $3.30 vs consensus $3.00, revenue $5.35bn vs $5.14bn. Sales growth expected in 2027 similar to 2026.
TEX Q3 EPS reported $1.50 vs consensus $1.42, sales $2.2bn vs $2.16bn. Full-year EPS guide narrowed to $4.80-5 from $4.70-5.10, sales $8-8.2bn. New $500mm buyback.
VRT Q3 EPS reported $2.21 vs consensus $1.82, revenue $4.3bn vs $3.75bn. Q4 guide: EPS $2.22-2.28 vs consensus $2.21, revenue $4.31-4.5bn vs $4.3bn. Full-year guidance raised.
Upcoming earnings this week: 10/29 pre-market includes CARR, CRH, HWM, LIN, TT, TXT and others. 10/29 post-market includes IR, FMC, RSG. 10/30 pre-market includes GD, NVT, LYB.
